paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. The gospel Paul preached was not made up by a man. He says, "I received it by revelation from Jesus Christ" (Galatians 1:12). That matters to you, because the good news you're standing on didn't come from somebody's clever idea or a committee meeting. It came from Jesus Himself.

Now look at who God picked to carry it. Paul was the man who "severely" persecuted the church and tried to destroy it (Galatians 1:13). But God had set him apart from his mother's womb and called him by His grace (Galatians 1:15). I think that means nobody is too far gone for God to reach, and nobody is too far gone to be used by Him. If God can reach Paul running the wrong way, friend, He can reach you, and I know a little something about being pulled out of a place where you figured you were done!

And see what the people did when they heard about it. The churches of Judea had never met Paul, but they heard what happened to him, and "they glorified God because of me" (Galatians 1:24). When God changes a life, the glory goes to God. So let the Word do its work in you, and let your story point people to Him too.
